verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev workflows are code-defined tasks. Its official MCP server lets an AI assistant initialize projects, deploy them to environments and trigger runs, which roughly covers an agent creating, updating and activating workflows. A management API with secret-key/PAT auth also exists, but the evidence never shows public REST endpoints that create or update task definitions, and probes found no OpenAPI spec. missing for 10: documented public API endpoints to create/update/activate workflow definitions, an OpenAPI spec, and hands-on corroboration of agent-driven deploys.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent create, update, and activate a workflow programmatically through the public API

citations.quote: Initialize new Trigger.dev projects, List and manage your projects and organizations, Get task information and trigger task runs, Deploy projects to different environments
Give your AI assistant direct access to Trigger.dev tools — search docs, trigger tasks, deploy projects, and monitor runs.
There are two methods of authenticating with the management API: using a named API key associated with a specific environment in a project (`secretKey`), or using a personal access token
